thread:
leo: pager-bot alerted: sudden jump in 5xx + cross-region traffic from eu-west starting ~10:05 UTC. looks like smart-routing is bouncing requests during failover.
pager-bot: HIGH SEV: /v1/chat generate 5xx rate >15% in eu-west since 10:05 UTC. auto-paging leo (on-call).
anya: i can see a fanout to us-central and ap-south as fallbacks. weirdly, fallbacks include several variants with suffix '-canary-fallback'.
matt: that suffix was only supposed to be used in staging. did a policy push accidentally include it in prod?
tasha: check recent policy commits. git log shows PR #1987 merged 09:58 by infra-automation: "add generic fallback pattern for temporary variants". pattern: `.*-fallback$`.
leo: that wildcard means when a node fails, router will pick any variant that matches pattern across regions -> thundering herd.
anya: and on top of that, partner SDKs are retrying aggressively (no jitter). we're getting duplicate traffic multiplied across regions.
matt: supporting evidence: request_id dump shows identical client-retry chains hitting eu-west then us-central then ap-south within 300ms windows.
infra-bot: note: config-change pr #1987 reached prod at 10:00 UTC. rollback available.
leo: immediate mitigation proposals: (1) roll back PR #1987, (2) apply temporary route block to disallow cross-region fallbacks, (3) apply rate limiting for offending client ids, (4) notify partner to throttle retries.
tasha: i'm taking (2) and (1) in parallel. applying route-block now: `router.set.allow_cross_region_fallback(false)`.
(20s)
tasha: route-block applied. cross-region fallback attempts dropped by ~92% in the last minute.
matt: rolling back PR #1987 now. deploy pipeline shows green.
infra-bot: rollback deploy completed at 10:11:06 UTC. wildcard fallback removed.
leo: good. next: we still see elevated retry volume from partner p-893. can we enforce backoff at edge?
anya: adding per-customer throttle: `limit(p-893)=40rps; client_retry_penalty=3s`. pushing rule.
(10s)
anya: throttle in place. repeated client retries now return 429/Retry-After for aggressive behavior.
support-bot: open tickets surfaced: T-4521, T-4526, T-4528 — three customers reporting generation errors and timeouts starting 10:06 UTC.
leo: update customer comms: sending short note acknowledging incident and immediate remediation. include suggested client-side backoff config: exponential backoff starting 500ms + jitter.
(quiet)
anya: metrics: eu-west error rate fell from 18% -> 6% after route-block + throttle. p95 latency improved by ~1.4s.
matt: additional hardening we should do in follow-up: 1) disable wildcard fallback patterns in prod by policy, 2) add a config lint that forbids regex fallback without allowlist, 3) add router-level debounce to avoid fanout during short transient failures, 4) create synthetic test that simulates client retry storms across regions. I'll open PRs.
tasha: ops runbook update idea: when routing policy changes, enforce canary + traffic threshold checks to avoid global fanout.
leo: agree. also add server-side exponential damping: if same request signature retries across N nodes in T seconds, drop to 503 with Retry-After.
anya: quick patch: enable retry-damping heuristic on router for next 2 hours. will monitor.
(30s)
anya: damping enabled. duplicate request signature counts decreased, overall error rate now 2.1% and token throughput stable.
leo: ok marking pager resolved locally but keep monitoring for 30m. can someone capture timeline and impact numbers?
matt: grabbing numbers: incident window ~10:05-10:12 UTC; peak 5xx 22% at 10:07; affected customers 3; mitigation steps: route-block, rollback PR #1987, throttles for p-893, retry-damping, cache enabled for hot prompts of affected customers.
leo: great. follow-up action items: A) permanently remove wildcard fallback ability in policy language, B) require code review + manual approval for fallback changes, C) add client SDK guidance and contact partner p-893, D) add router telemetry for cross-region-fallback spikes. assign owners?
matt: A+B -> me. tasha: C -> tasha + support. anya: D -> anya.
leo: thanks all. drafting RCA and customer messages now. closing thread in 1 hour if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
